scenes.visual: Hook before the title: one large grey schematic neuron fills the frame. Four locked cards orbit it: identity, projection, birth window, ancestry. Question marks pulse. On-screen label: schematic. Colour map for both chapters: blue equals observed labels and tracers; gold equals time pulse; green equals inherited mark or reporter; red equals intervention or deletion; grey equals unobserved cells and DNA.

scenes.tts: A finished neuron hides its past. Which label could reveal the part you need in that tissue? Its shape alone cannot show its birth time, ancestry, or distant projection. Each question needs an event that can carry that information forward.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the neuron. Its visible outline stays fixed while the four cards slide behind it, still locked. A moving thread reaches from each card toward a different part of the cell, then stops before connecting. Keep the schematic label visible.
scenes.narration: A finished neuron hides its past. Which label could reveal the part you need in that tissue? Its shape alone cannot show its birth time, ancestry, or distant projection. Each question needs an event that can carry that information forward.

scenes.visual: Brief title over the carried neuron: What Can a Label Prove? The four cards remain behind the title and drift slowly.

scenes.tts: Start with identity. A Nissl stain reveals many cell bodies. A Golgi stain fills a few cells and their branches. An antibody binds one chosen protein. These marks report what they detect, not when the cells formed.
scenes.visual: Transform the neuron into one field of six grey cells. Blue Nissl shading appears around every nucleus. It clears; one cell fills blue through its branches for Golgi. It clears; a blue protein badge appears only in two cells for antibody detection. The gold birth card stays locked.
scenes.narration: Start with identity. A Nissl stain reveals many cell bodies. A Golgi stain fills a few cells and their branches. An antibody binds one chosen protein. These marks report what they detect, not when the cells formed.

scenes.tts: For a projection, use the neuron's own transport. Put a tracer near cell bodies, and anterograde transport carries it toward terminals. Put a retrograde tracer at a target, and terminals carry it back. The result maps a sampled population, not every synapse.
scenes.visual: Carry one neuron into a wide layout. Blue particles travel from its soma to three terminals under an anterograde arrow. Reset the particles. Move a blue injection spot to one target, then animate particles back to two somata. Leave a third projecting cell grey to show incomplete sampling.
scenes.narration: For a projection, use the neuron's own transport. Put a tracer near cell bodies, and anterograde transport carries it toward terminals. Put a retrograde tracer at a target, and terminals carry it back. The result maps a sampled population, not every synapse.

scenes.tts: Birth-dating follows a different event. During a short pulse, tritiated thymidine or B R D U enters D N A being synthesized. In a dividing cell, that means ess phase. The pulse marks a cohort copying D N A during that window.
scenes.caption: Birth-dating follows a different event. During a short pulse, tritiated thymidine or BrdU enters DNA being synthesized. In a dividing cell, that means S phase. The pulse marks a cohort copying DNA during that window.
scenes.visual: Transform the axon into a gold timeline with a narrow pulse window. Three grey progenitor circles cross the window. Gold dots enter their simple DNA bars only while each bar is copying. A bracket labelled cohort closes around those three cells.
scenes.narration: Birth-dating follows a different event. During a short pulse, tritiated thymidine or BrdU enters DNA being synthesized. In a dividing cell, that means S phase. The pulse marks a cohort copying DNA during that window.

scenes.tts: After the pulse comes the chase. Each further division usually dilutes label among the descendants. Heavy label later supports few additional divisions and an approximate last ess phase. Weak label fits continued cycling, although uptake and detection also vary.
scenes.caption: After the pulse comes the chase. Each further division usually dilutes label among the descendants. Heavy label later supports few additional divisions and an approximate last S phase. Weak label fits continued cycling, although uptake and detection also vary.
scenes.visual: The gold timeline moves right. One labelled cell stops dividing and keeps a dense gold bar. Another divides twice; its gold dots dilute schematically among four daughters. A balance gauge, marked schematic, compares heavy and weak signal. Add the label approximate, not exact.
scenes.narration: After the pulse comes the chase. Each further division usually dilutes label among the descendants. Heavy label later supports few additional divisions and an approximate last S phase. Weak label fits continued cycling, although uptake and detection also vary.

scenes.tts: Ancestry needs a mark that survives division. A grafted quail nucleus stays recognizable in chick tissue. A retroviral insert enters a dividing cell's D N A. Cree can permanently switch on a reporter. In each case, descendants inherit a durable difference.
scenes.caption: Ancestry needs a mark that survives division. A grafted quail nucleus stays recognizable in chick tissue. A retroviral insert enters a dividing cell's DNA. Cre can permanently switch on a reporter. In each case, descendants inherit a durable difference.
scenes.visual: Replace the timeline with one green-marked founder. First, its nucleus gets a green quail pattern and moves into a grey tissue. Next, a green retroviral block joins its DNA bar. Finally, a green reporter lamp switches on. Each version branches into a small marked family tree.
scenes.narration: Ancestry needs a mark that survives division. A grafted quail nucleus stays recognizable in chick tissue. A retroviral insert enters a dividing cell's DNA. Cre can permanently switch on a reporter. In each case, descendants inherit a durable difference.

scenes.tts: Predict the next frame. One founder carries a permanent D N A change, then divides twice. Which cells should carry that change?
scenes.caption: Predict the next frame. One founder carries a permanent DNA change, then divides twice. Which cells should carry that change?
scenes.visual: Hold one green-marked founder above an empty two-generation family tree. Three answer outlines glow faintly: founder only, one branch, every descendant. Do not reveal the answer.
scenes.narration: Predict the next frame. One founder carries a permanent DNA change, then divides twice. Which cells should carry that change?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Keep the founder and empty family tree on screen. A four-and-a-half-second ring closes slowly around the three possible answers.

scenes.tts: Every descendant inherits the changed D N A. Yet one colour across many founders gives a population fate map, not separate clones. Sparse induction, multiple colours, or distinct barcodes can separate neighbouring families.
scenes.caption: Every descendant inherits the changed DNA. Yet one colour across many founders gives a population fate map, not separate clones. Sparse induction, multiple colours, or distinct barcodes can separate neighbouring families.
scenes.visual: Grow four green descendants from the founder and copy the green mark into each DNA bar. Then zoom out to several green founders whose trees overlap. Reset and recolour each founder family differently, separating the trees.
scenes.narration: Every descendant inherits the changed DNA. Yet one colour across many founders gives a population fate map, not separate clones. Sparse induction, multiple colours, or distinct barcodes can separate neighbouring families.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. A tool supports only what its mark records. Protein binding can report target detection. Transport can report a projection. D N A synthesis can date a cohort approximately. An inherited D N A change can report ancestry.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule. A tool supports only what its mark records. Protein binding can report target detection. Transport can report a projection. DNA synthesis can date a cohort approximately. An inherited DNA change can report ancestry.
scenes.visual: Bring back the four cards around the same neuron. A blue protein badge unlocks identity only as far as target detected. Moving blue tracer unlocks projection. Gold pulse unlocks birth window. Green branching mark unlocks ancestry. Each carrier physically enters its matching card.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. A tool supports only what its mark records. Protein binding can report target detection. Transport can report a projection. DNA synthesis can date a cohort approximately. An inherited DNA change can report ancestry.

scenes.tts: The rule also tells you when to stop. A tracer does not prove every synapse. A weak birth label is not a precise birthday. A shared lineage colour may hide many founders. State the strongest claim, then name the limit.
scenes.visual: Each unlocked card expands, then a boundary line stops it from covering the other cards. Under identity, show target only. Under projection, show population only. Under birth, show approximate. Under ancestry, show founders unresolved. The limits settle beside their claims.
scenes.narration: The rule also tells you when to stop. A tracer does not prove every synapse. A weak birth label is not a precise birthday. A shared lineage colour may hide many founders. State the strongest claim, then name the limit.

scenes.visual: End card: A tool supports only what its mark records. The neuron remains behind it with slow movement.
